claims.text: Geometric overflow is a boundary-based formulation of hallucination in large language models.
Geometric overflow is defined as boundary violation under preserved internal coherence.
Geometric overflow isolates a failure regime in which outputs remain fluent, internally stable, and high-confidence while violating externally defined constraints.
Boundary tension measures proximity to admissibility boundaries.
Boundary tension enables detection of limit-state behavior preceding overflow.
Geometric overflow is orthogonal to model calibration.
Even perfectly calibrated models may exhibit coherent boundary crossing.
Regime separability exists between overflow and collapse in a retrieval-augmented question answering setting.

evidence.description: Mathematical proof showing that overflow is orthogonal to calibration.
Mathematical proof establishing that perfectly calibrated models can exhibit coherent boundary crossing.
A minimal empirical illustration in a retrieval-augmented question answering setting.

methodologies.name: Geometric Overflow and Boundary Tension Diagnostics
methodologies.description: A theoretical framework defining an admissible manifold induced by external constraints and using boundary tension to measure proximity to admissibility boundaries.

limitations.text: Existing hallucination analysis perspectives (probabilistic miscalibration, distributional shift, generalization error) do not explicitly distinguish between internal representational instability and externally grounded boundary violations.
